attack_summary: Independently re-derived every count via python3 over quran-verses.json (6236 verses) and cross-checked against the corpus morphology cache and the Uthmani text. All two empirical load-bearing claims confirmed; no counterexample found even under aggressive orthographic normalization.

checks.claim: Exact contiguous 4-word phrase 'رب اني ظلمت نفسي' occurs in exactly 2 verses
checks.method: whitespace-token sequence match on textSimple; repeated on Uthmani text and with alif/hamza/ya-maqsura/ta-marbuta normalization
checks.result: {27:44, 28:16} — CONFIRMED (identical result across textSimple, Uthmani, and normalized variants)

checks.claim: 2-word core 'ظلمت نفسي' occurs only in the same 2 verses
checks.method: token-sequence match + broadened substring 'ظلمت نفس' to catch any possessor (نفسي/نفسك/نفسه/نفسها)
checks.result: {27:44, 28:16} — CONFIRMED; broadened possessor sweep also yields only these 2

checks.claim: The lone third 'ظلمت' token (10:54) is not a counterexample
checks.result: 10:54 = ظَلَمَتْ PERF 3FS ('a soul that wronged'), NOT 1S, and not followed by نفسي (reads 'نفس ظلمت ما في الارض'). Correctly excluded. Both target verses are ظَلَمْتُ PERF|VF:1|1S = 'I wronged'.

checks.claim: Speaker of 27:44 is the Queen of Sheba
checks.result: CONFIRMED — 'قالت رب اني ظلمت نفسي واسلمت مع سليمان' (feminine 'she said'); scene is the Queen entering Sulayman's glass palace. Sun-worship origin grounded in 27:24 'يسجدون للشمس'; disbelieving people in 27:43.

checks.claim: Speaker of 28:16 is Musa, immediately after killing the Egyptian, before prophethood
checks.result: CONFIRMED — 28:15 'فوكزه موسى فقضى عليه' (Musa strikes and kills); 28:16 is the confession directly after. Commissioning at the bush (28:29-30) comes only after flight to Madyan, so he is not yet a prophet. Quran-grounded, no hadith.
CONFIRMED — surah 27 precedes 28. Thesis explicitly scopes ordering to 'mushaf order,' so the historical fact that Musa predates Sulayman does not refute it.

checks.claim: Distinct from 7:23 (plural 'ظلمنا انفسنا', Adam+wife) and 21:87 (Yunus, 'اني كنت من الظالمين')
checks.result: CONFIRMED — 7:23 is the plural first-person, different phrase; 21:87 uses a different construction. Neither collides with the singular exact phrase.

PASS — phrase, both speakers, sun-worship, killing, pre-prophetic status, and submission are all in the text. Only the proper name 'Bilqis' is extra-Quranic (tafsir), and it is incidental, not load-bearing.

ADJACENT BUT DISTINCT — published zulm-al-nafs-wronging-the-self covers the concept; bilqis-* cover throne/letter/leadership; musa-burning-bush covers the commissioning (28:29+), not the killing/confession. None pairs the two speakers on the identical exact phrase. Novel angle stands.

required_corrections: None load-bearing. Editorial soft spots to tighten before publish: (1) 'Bilqis' is a tafsir name, not Quranic — either drop it or flag it as traditional; the Quran identifies her only as the Queen of Sheba who and whose people prostrate to the sun (27:24). (2) 'Pagan queen' — she utters the line in the very act of submitting (27:44 'واسلمت'); frame paganism as her STARTING POINT (the reveal), not her status mid-sentence, or a pedant will object she is already converting. (3) Anchor 'four words' explicitly to the Arabic (رب/اني/ظلمت/نفسي); the English gloss is longer, so 'four words' only holds in Arabic. (4) Keep the 'mushaf order' qualifier prominent — historically Musa precedes Sulayman by generations, so avoid any 'first/then' phrasing that implies chronological firstness. (5) Differentiate the piece explicitly from published zulm-al-nafs-wronging-the-self and the bilqis pieces to avoid cannibalization. (6) Optional pre-empt: 12:53 ('ما ابري نفسي', disputed speaker) and 7:23 (plural, Adam+wife) are near-cousins but NOT the same phrase — naming them shows the 'only these two' claim is airtight.
notes: The two empirical claims that carry the piece are exactly correct and robust under textSimple, Uthmani, and aggressive normalization. Morphology confirms both verbs are 1S perfect. Narrative framing is Quran-grounded. No refuting counterexample exists. Survives with editorial-only corrections.
